note: Indirect and stack rows (pdf 55): the effective address is held in register MMM (Fig 3.2.4, pdf 48). R1-R3 never change, R4 and R5 post-increment, R6 post-increments on output (push) and pre-decrements on input (pull), all 16-bit wrapping (C17, POL-STK-01). Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation. Bus offsets follow the indirect read figure (pdf 29) and the MVO write figure (pdf 31); the pull read offset is inference (C36).

vectors.derivation: The indirect table (pdf 55) prints PSHR SSS as 1001 110 SSS, 9 cycles, 'PuSH data from Register SSS to the stack', no status change; the table header says MMM = 6 for MVO is post increment R6. Fig 3.2.4 (pdf 48), MMM = 110 for MVO only: PC <- PC+1, EA <- (MMM), (MMM) <- (MMM)+1. S3.4.6 (pdf 62): the data is placed in the cell R6 names and then R6 is incremented by one (C17 resolved). SSS = 001 (R1 = $A5C3), R6 = $02F0: the word at $02F0 becomes $A5C3, then R6 = $02F0 + 1 = $02F1. The write is at the old R6, not at $02EF (a pre-decrement would write there and leave R6 = $02EF). PC: $1000 -> $1001. Flags: S = Z = OV = C = 1 stay 1 (no status change). C56: the manual is silent on the MVO family's interruptibility and the default makes it non-interruptible, so prev_interruptible goes 1 -> 0. Bus (pdf 31, MVO timing (write operation), 9 cycles: BAR, NACT, DTB, NACT, BAR, NACT, DW, DWS, NACT; the second BAR puts out the effective address): FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, then the WRITE at cycle 4. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.derivation: The indirect table (pdf 55) prints PULR DDD as 1010 110 DDD, 11 cycles, 'PULl data from the stack to Register DDD', no status change; the table header says other instructions pre-decrement R6. Fig 3.2.4 (pdf 48), MMM = 110 for non-MVO: PC <- PC+1, (MMM) <- (MMM)-1, EA <- (MMM). S3.4.6 (pdf 62): R6 is first decremented, then the data is fetched from the cell R6 names (C17 resolved). DDD = 010 (R2), R6 = $02F1: R6 = $02F1 - 1 = $02F0, then R2 = the word at $02F0 = $5A3C. The word at the old R6 ($02F1) is never read (a post-decrement would read it). PC: $1000 -> $1001. Cycles: the printed 11, which is the MVI@ base 8 plus the '*Add 3 to number of cycles if MMM=6' footnote (pdf 55); this is the A-13 witness of MVI@'s MMM = 6 branch. Flags: S = Z = OV = C = 1 stay 1 (no status change). The row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible goes 0 -> 1. Bus (inference, C36): FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, then one READ at the decremented R6. No figure prints a pull; the core puts its BAR at cycle 7, after the 3 extra cycles, so the cycle is not asserted. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.derivation: Two units. Step 1, PSHR R1 (1001 110 001, pdf 55, 9 cycles): R1 = $BEEF is written at R6 = $02F0, then R6 = $02F1, PC $1000 -> $1001; the MVO family is non-interruptible by the C56 default. Step 2, PULR R5 (1010 110 101, pdf 55, 11 cycles): R6 = $02F1 - 1 = $02F0, then R5 = the word at $02F0 = $BEEF, PC $1001 -> $1002; PULR is interruptible, so prev_interruptible ends 1. S3.4.6 (pdf 62): the push places data and then increments R6, the pull decrements R6 and then fetches, so a push followed by a pull returns the pushed value and restores R6 to $02F0 (C17 resolved). Cycles 9 + 11 = 20. Flags stay 0 (neither row changes status). Bus (inference for the pull, C36): FETCH $1000 at 0, WRITE $02F0 at 4 (pdf 31), FETCH $1001 at 9, then one READ of $02F0 in the second unit. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
